milestones.description: Uses position_near_with_facing because this is a find/locate task. The birch saplings are at (8,0,-8) in the NE corner (~11.3 blocks from spawn). Max_distance=12 ensures the player must navigate toward the saplings, and facing_tolerance=60 confirms visual observation.

Uses position_near_with_facing because this is a find/locate task. The stone platform at (-6,0,-7) hosts the stonecutter and crafting table. Max_distance=10 ensures meaningful navigation from spawn (~9.2 blocks away).

Uses position_near_with_facing because this is a find/locate task. The pyramid front face at (0,0,10) has smooth_quartz_slabs. Max_distance=10 ensures the player walks most of the 10 blocks south from spawn to observe the pyramid.

Uses position_near_with_facing because this is a find/locate task. The potted orange tulip is at (-3,0,-3), only ~4.2 blocks from spawn. Max_distance=5 and facing_tolerance=45 are tight to ensure the player deliberately walks toward it and faces it directly rather than triggering from spawn.

Uses position_near_with_facing because this is a find/locate task. Target is the far end of the carpet path at (0,0,8). Max_distance=8 means the player must walk south along the carpet to satisfy this — from spawn (distance=8) they are exactly at the boundary, requiring at least a few steps forward.

Uses inventory_has because mining a potted plant drops a flower_pot item into the player's inventory. This directly confirms the block was actually broken rather than relying on block absence which could be a command failure.

Uses position_near_with_facing with tight max_distance=3 because the system cannot directly detect UI interaction. The stonecutter is at (-7,1,-7). Being within 3 blocks and facing it is the closest proxy for right-click interaction given system constraints — the player must be close enough to actually interact.

Uses inventory_has because the crafted jungle trapdoor ends up in the player's inventory. Recipe: 4-6 jungle planks → 2 trapdoors. Checking for at least 1 in inventory is the definitive confirmation that crafting succeeded.
Uses inventory_has because the crafted blue carpet ends up in the player's inventory. Recipe: 2 blue_wool → 3 blue_carpet. Checking for at least 1 confirms crafting succeeded.
Uses inventory_has because the crafted yellow stained glass ends up in the player's inventory. Recipe: 8 glass + 1 yellow_dye → 8 yellow_stained_glass. Chest provides exactly these materials.

Uses count_in_box_at_least (kind='block') because lighting up the pyramid requires placing torch blocks inside the interior. The box [-2,1,11] to [2,3,15] covers the carved-out 5x3x5 interior space. Requiring 3 torches confirms meaningful illumination. Torches placed on the solid quartz floor appear at y=1.

Uses count_in_box_at_most (kind='mob', max_count=0) because killing the vex means it no longer exists. A very generous box (±20 XZ, -5 to +15 Y, -5 to +30 Z) is used because vexes phase through blocks and fly far from spawn. The box must be large enough that the vex stays inside until actually killed, preventing false positives from the mob simply walking out.
